title: Rate-limiting and anti-enumeration on the sign-in flow are delegated to Clerk
iWant: the project to leave rate-limiting and anti-enumeration to Clerk rather than layering a second rate limiter on top
soThat: the sign-in surface's rate-limit behaviour is one system's behaviour and does not confuse users with two competing back-off timers

acceptanceCriteria.description: The project's sign-in surface applies no project-authored rate limiter, throttle, or enumeration defence to the sign-in POST or its equivalent Clerk-initiated flow.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the project's request-handling surface for the sign-in route(s) that front Clerk's sign-in flow
acceptanceCriteria.when: a source-tree scan enumerates rate-limit middleware, throttle wrappers, or enumeration-defence checks bound to the sign-in surface
acceptanceCriteria.then: the scan returns zero matches on the sign-in surface; the same scan on other surfaces (a public API, a webhook receiver) is unaffected by this AC

acceptanceCriteria.description: Repeated sign-in attempts against the project's Clerk development instance exhibit Clerk's documented rate-limit behaviour, not a project-authored variant.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a burst of N sign-in attempts (N chosen to exceed Clerk's documented per-address threshold for the strategy) against the project's Clerk-development instance
acceptanceCriteria.when: the burst is dispatched and the responses are collected
acceptanceCriteria.then: the observed refusal shape (status code, response body error identifier, retry-after header if any) matches Clerk's documented rate-limit response for the strategy; no project-authored refusal shape appears in the burst
